_comment: The installer never applies this. Wiring a hook into settings.json is a manual, deliberate step you take yourself. Copy the entries you want into your own settings.json 'hooks' block, adjusting the script path to where this repo ended up on disk.

suggestions.purpose: Scans the tool input for credential-shaped strings (cloud keys, tokens, private-key blocks) before the write or command runs. Exits 2 to block if it finds one.
Denies direct edits to .env* and .credentials.json files outright, regardless of content. Reading key names for a capability sweep still works via grep.
suggestions.exitCodes: always 0; blocking is expressed as a JSON permissionDecision: deny

suggestions.purpose: Blocks a fixed list of dangerous shell patterns before they run: recursive force-delete, a force-push to main or master, a wrangler pages secret delete, DROP TABLE/DATABASE, recursive chmod 777, a find -delete against a root path, and a fork bomb.

Runs a fast syntax check on the file just written: node --check for .js/.cjs/.mjs, py_compile for .py, a JSON parse for .json. Reports a failure as a system reminder instead of silently leaving a broken file behind.

manualChecks.purpose: AST-validates a PowerShell script with the PowerShell parser. Not wired as a hook; run it by hand or from your own CI on any .ps1 file before you ship it, per naming.conventions.md's ASCII-only rule for .ps1/.bat files.
Stage 1 of the self-harness loop. Read-only, scans your own trace store for recurring failure clusters. Meant to run on a weekly schedule you set up yourself, not as a tool-event hook.
